title: 2027-08-03-ingress-patterns-and-dynamic-burst-scoping-lighthouse-payments
summary: POC scoping to capture Lighthouse Payments' ingestion/ingress burst patterns, token mix, and success criteria. Agreement to run a 4-week pilot with benchmark week in week 2. Redwood to provide replay harness and benchmark template; Lighthouse to share 7-day sample traffic and auth-safe prompts. Key success metrics: p95 latency, p99 tail, error rate <0.1%, and cost per 1M tokens within target range.
topics: QPS vs concurrency vs connection spikes
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-03 15:00 PDT
Duration: 63 minutes
Attendees: Samir, Claire, Diego (Redwood); Jorge, Maya, Priya, Ethan (Lighthouse)

Auto-summary: agree to pilot with traffic replay and bench week; collect traces; share security docs.

00:00:05 Samir: hey everyone, thanks for taking time. quick intro from our side — i'm Samir, AE on the account, and Claire and Diego are our SEs. you all?
00:00:14 Jorge: hi, i'm Jorge, lead eng on payment flows. maya product, priya security, ethan is SRE.
00:00:22 Samir: great. the purpose today is to nail the workload profile — we need QPS, bursts, tokens per request, p95/p99 targets, and constraints for private deploy / VPC. we'll scope a POC around that.
00:00:39 Maya: yes, main ask is: we have a mix of short auth checks and longer reconciliation prompts. typical short flow is like 15-40 input tokens and 10-30 output tokens; long reconciliation is 200-400 in, 400-1,200 out. averages are hard to pin.
00:00:58 Claire: ok that variability matters because it changes token throughput and effective concurrency. can you share sample percentiles? average, 50/90/99?
00:01:07 Jorge: rough numbers — mean QPS about 12, concurrency 4-6 most hours, but we have spikes to ~180-220 QPS during settlement windows and marketing promos. bursts last 3-7 minutes usually.
00:01:24 Diego: and are spikes sudden spikes or ramped?
00:01:28 Ethan: mostly sudden, like within 30-60s, sometimes incremental over a few minutes. we'll annotate logs.
00:01:35 Samir: that's good. Redwood's continuous batching and prefix caching help, but extreme suddenness forces us to size for burst headroom or provide graceful fallback. what's your tolerance for degraded latency during bursts?
00:01:49 Maya: product prefers p95 < 300ms for auth checks; p99 for short checks ideally < 600ms. longer reconciliation can be more lenient — p95 < 2s, p99 < 5s. error budget under 0.1% per day.
00:02:04 Claire: noted. for benchmarking, we'll separate short vs long prompt profiles and run isolated tests + mixed replay to capture interference.
00:02:12 Priya: on security: we need VPC peering, customer-managed KMS for key material, and SOC 2 + ISO overview. is Redwood's private offering required, or can hosted with VPC suffice?
00:02:25 Samir: both options on table. hosted with VPC peering is our fastest path; private deployment gives you full control and HSM/KMS routing. we'll share the security pack.
00:02:34 Priya: also audit logs retention — we need 1 year for certain streams, but can start with 90 days for the pilot.
00:02:41 Diego: we can enable extended retention as an add-on; we'll include cost in the POC estimate.
00:02:46 Jorge: on cost, what's typical for a workload like ours? high token variance.
00:02:51 Claire: rough math — if average tokens per request is 300 and you do 12 QPS sustained, that's about 311M tokens/day; pricing depends on model variant + quantization. for pilot we recommend a 2-model approach: one low-latency small model for auth checks and a larger quality model for reconciliation with fallback routing.
00:03:12 Maya: fallback routing meaning if dedicated capacity maxes out, we go to a slightly cheaper hosted region?
00:03:17 Samir: yes, or to a quantized variant with lower compute. automatic fallback policies are configurable.
00:03:22 Ethan: can Redwood throttle or queue gracefully for us? we don't want dropped payments if the model is slow.
00:03:28 Diego: we support durable queuing and throttles. you can set timeouts and queue depth; we also have circuit-breaker style fallbacks to simpler deterministic logic if latency passes threshold.
00:03:40 Jorge: okay good. let's talk metrics and benchmark design.
00:03:43 Claire: plan: week 0-1 setup and data collection, week 2 benchmark (replay harness runs synthetic + real traces), week 3 tuning (batching, quantization), week 4 validation and decision. Bench phase will measure p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, cost per 1M tokens, and error rate.
00:04:04 Maya: we want a test that includes 10% of traffic as reconciliation to ensure interference. also include cold start scenarios.
00:04:11 Samir: yes, we'll simulate cold nodes and KV cache misses. for cold starts we expect tail latency increases; we'll measure warm vs cold delta.
00:04:20 Priya: any data residency issues? our merchant data must remain in us-east-1.
00:04:24 Samir: we'll pin region; that's supported.
00:04:27 Diego: quick question on tokenization — are you using UTF-8 heavy payloads? special chars?
00:04:32 Jorge: yes we have some merchant notes with emojis and non-ascii; average input tokenization increases ~10% vs char count.
00:04:40 Claire: we'll include tokenization step in the replay.
00:04:44 Maya: for success criteria, product needs: 1) auth p95 <300ms and <0.05% errors; 2) reconciliation p95 <2s on pilot baseline; 3) cost per 1M tokens within 15% of our budget target; 4) integration with our SSO and KMS.
00:05:07 Samir: great, we'll codify those. any legal/procurement requirements?
00:05:11 Priya: we need DPA language, subprocessor list, and contract review. procurement will engage if pilot shows positive results.
00:05:19 Diego: we'll share DPA and SOC pack.
00:05:22 Jorge: about telemetry: can we get per-route token-level cost breakdown and trace-level latency?
00:05:27 Claire: yes, per-route and per-token cost and sample traces. we'll also provide an ops dashboard you can run for the pilot.
00:05:33 Ethan: do you support offline replay, like doing a dry-run on our logs against a local model?
00:05:39 Samir: yes, Redwood provides a replay harness and a local runner for initial checks. for production-like numbers we run against our infra or your Private deployment.
00:05:47 Maya: is there a support SLA during pilot? we need faster escalation windows.
00:05:51 Samir: we'll assign a CSM and SE on-call for bench week; response times per agreement.
00:05:56 Priya: encryption at rest — we must ensure keys never leave our KMS.
00:05:59 Diego: with Private or dedicated, keys stay in your KMS; hosted VPC can be set up with customer-managed keys, depending on region.
00:06:09 Jorge: let's do numbers for capacity: if we wanted to tolerate a 220 QPS spike with 50ms average token latency, what sizing are we looking at?
00:06:17 Claire: rough back-of-envelope: depends on sequence length and model. For short auth (40 in / 20 out) you'd need smaller footprint; for mixed profile with 300 tokens average, you'd need more GPUs. we'll run detailed sizing once we have token distribution and 7-day trace.
00:06:31 Maya: who will run the replay? us or Redwood?
00:06:34 Samir: Redwood can run it, but we prefer you to sanitize and push traces to our secure bucket; Diego will walk through the anonymization script.
00:06:44 Diego: we'll provide a script that strips PII and replaces sensitive fields; it outputs a sample manifest.
00:06:49 Priya: need to review script before running.
00:06:52 Samir: understood.
00:06:55 Jorge: timeline check — we want pilot start in 2 weeks if possible.
00:06:59 Samir: feasible. week 0: onboarding and trace handoff; week 1: replay dry runs and model selection; week 2: benchmark; week 3: tuning; week 4: wrap and decision.
00:07:12 Maya: decision gate after week 4 with a scorecard.
00:07:15 Claire: we'll provide a scoring template (latency, errors, cost, ops friction).
00:07:20 Ethan: what about model variants and quantization — will you test int8 or nf4?
00:07:25 Diego: yes, we'll test a quantized variant (int8/nf4) to reduce token costs and compare quality with golden prompts.
00:07:33 Jorge: how do you measure quality regression?
00:07:35 Claire: we use a prompt set of critical flows and automated evals that score correctness and hallucination metrics; human spot checks for recon flows.
00:07:44 Maya: any upfront costs?
00:07:46 Samir: pilot credits cover bench runs; minimal setup fees for private deployments. we'll call out estimates in the POC statement.
00:07:54 Priya: ok procurement will look at that.
00:07:57 Samir: any more questions?
00:08:00 Jorge: can you run a quick demo of replay harness? maybe not today.
00:08:03 Claire: we can send a recorded walkthrough.
00:08:06 Diego: next steps recap in a sec.
00:08:09 Samir: let's recap and action items.
00:08:12 Claire: action item: Lighthouse to provide 7-day sanitized traffic sample and access (owner: Jorge) — due: 2027-08-10.
00:08:21 Claire: action item: Redwood to send replay harness repo + anonymization script (owner: Diego) — due: 2027-08-05.
00:08:29 Claire: action item: Redwood to share SOC2/ISO and DPA docs (owner: Samir) — due: 2027-08-04.
00:08:36 Claire: action item: Redwood to deliver benchmark plan + scoring template (owner: Claire) — due: 2027-08-05.
00:08:44 Maya: action item: internal procurement kickoff (owner: Maya / Priya) — due: 2027-08-12.
00:08:50 Samir: we'll schedule bench-week kickoff for 2027-08-17 if traces arrive by 8/10.
00:08:57 Ethan: confirmed tentative.
00:09:00 Samir: thanks all. we'll follow up with calendar invites and artifacts.
00:09:05 Jorge: thanks everyone, appreciate it.
